newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Over 200 killed in latest Sri Lanka rebel attack.
newsitem.headline: Over 200 killed in latest Sri Lanka rebel attack.

text.p: More than 200 soldiers and rebels were killed in the latest battle in northern Sri Lanka, where troops are fighting Tamil Tiger separatists in an attempt to open a key highway, the Defence Ministry said on Wednesday.

"Four officers and 60 soldiers were killed in action and 68 soldiers were wounded in the confrontation," a Defence Ministry statement said. "According to ground troops over 150 terrorists were killed and a large number injured."

It added that more than 1,000 Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels attacked the military's artillery and mortar positions near Periyamadu, north of the government-held town of Vavuniya, late on Tuesday.
Vavuniya lies some 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo.
But the Defence Ministry said the attack, the LTTE's second in two weeks, failed to capture artillery and cut off supplies to troops who are fighting farther north in the Puliyankulam area.
The rebels are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in mainly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east.
Some of the LTTE's suicide bombers killed themselves when troops opened fire, the Ministry added.
"Human waves of terrorists were severely beaten by the troops inflicting heavy casualties," the statement said.
The LTTE's spokesman in London, contacted by Reuters, said details of the attack had not yet reached him.
Independent confirmation of events is not possible as international media are not allowed in the battle zone.
Military officials in the north told Reuters the rebels managed to capture a five-inch mortar gun and about 100 small firearms in the five-hour battle.
They said the rebels had punched a hole between half to one kilometre (quarter to half a mile) wide in the military's defence line.
Air force jets and helicopter gunships were called in to strike rebel mortar positions while reinforcements rushed to assist ground troops, the Defence Ministry said.
Some 20,000 troops resumed Operation "Jaya Sikuru", or "Sure of Victory", on Monday from the Periyamadu area to open the highway to Jaffna peninsula.

Jaffna city was controlled by the rebels for nearly a decade before being captured by government forces last year. The rebels have now set up their base in the Wanni region just south of the peninsula.
Two weeks ago, the rebels mounted a similar daring attack on the military's rear near Vavuniya, delaying the main offensive.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
